items.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020
items.q: But both of those — because my aunt was a very elegant person. So that’s why he called her “Miss Fine.”

ctx.x: What about song titles? Did he ever have music that he had written, original music, that he had trouble thinking what do I call this?

Well it’s interesting, he would think of those when they had to go on a record. But I’ve got a ton of scores of N-201s and 302s and that kind of, and I have to sit down and figure out a lot of times what they were. And some of this stuff has never been done. And I’ve got boxes and boxes of music and I’ve had one of my students kind of help me catalogue stuff but then Covid came around so she can’t even come to the house anymore. But most of the stuff he had a good name for. That book of eleven songs, he had one…

In our collection at the college I have a score your dad did for Joe Williams, and so nothing seemed to faze him. I wonder, did he seem compelled to take every offer given to him? © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
